newsitem.title: USA: U.S. W.Coast crude prices fall as traders golf.
newsitem.headline: U.S. W.Coast crude prices fall as traders golf.

text.p: Crude oil prices on the U.S. West Coast sunk in line with marker crude values East of the Rockies on a combination of bearish news on Iraq and the weekly report from the American Petroleum Institute.
Trading on the Coast was virtually non-existant, however, as most of the major players were at a golfing outing hosted by Arco Pipeline Co, a unit of Atlantic Richfield Co (ARCO).

With ARCO and BP Oil traders out, the two main sellers of regional benchmark Alaska North Slope (ANS) were not in the market. A BP trader said, from the golf course, that ANS was still offered at $1.60 below WTI. The last reported trade was on May 23 at $1.75 below.
Buyers expected the next cargo to sell at $1.90-$2.00 off July WTI.

Major buyers were mostly either at the golf outing or, in the case of Tosco Corp, setting the July buying program. (Tosco crude traders recently moved to Pheonix, Arizona as part of the consolidation after the purchase of Unocal's downstream assets).

ANS outright prices tumbled 90 cents a barrel on the day in line with WTI as the U.S. confirmed it will vote to renew the United Nations "oil-for-food" deal with Iraq. Also, in after-hours trading, WTI was hit further by a bearish report showing a sharp crude stocks build even while refinery runs surged and gasoline production hit a record 8.195 million barrels per day (bpd) nationwide.
